This market rebound followed comments from US President Donald Trump indicating that military action against Iran is currently unnecessary, which helped alleviate global economic anxieties.

Broad-based buying lifted numerous key sectors in Pakistan, including automobile assemblers, commercial banks, cement producers, oil and gas exploration firms, oil marketing companies, and power generation units. Major index-heavy corporations such as MARI, OGDC, PPL, PSO, HUBCO, HBL, MCB, MEBL, and UBL all saw positive trading activity. Prior to this session, the exchange had wrapped up its strongest weekly rally in roughly six months.

Globally, Asian markets also climbed as crude oil prices retreated significantly. Brent crude futures dropped one percent to $91.56 per barrel, hitting their lowest mark since early September. Investors reacted positively to the prospect of potential diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran, easing fears of sustained inflation and high interest rates stemming from the conflict that began in late February.

Market analysts note that while these developments signal a possible path toward de-escalation, a considerable distance remains between ongoing diplomacy and a formal peace agreement. Meanwhile, stock indexes across Asia and the United States posted strong gains, though upcoming corporate earnings reports from technology firms focusing on artificial intelligence infrastructure remain a crucial upcoming test for investors.

stories.title: Pakistan Attracts Over $700 Million in Foreign Investment for Government Securities
stories.summary:
Foreign financial inflows into Pakistan's government securities surpassed $700 million during the first four months of the 2026-27 fiscal year, driven by some of the highest domestic returns in the region. Data from the State Bank of Pakistan indicates that foreign investors poured over $500 million into Pakistan Investment Bonds between July and October, alongside $238 million directed into treasury bills. This strong investor interest comes even as the State Bank of Pakistan raised its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent on October 26. Total foreign capital entering domestic bonds and the equity market reached $872 million during the four-month period. The United Arab Emirates emerged as the largest contributor to PIB investments, committing $395.7 million despite facing domestic economic strains resulting from the Gulf conflict that began in late February. Bahrain contributed the second-largest investment of $80 million in PIBs while also putting $72 million into T-bills. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom led participation in treasury bills by investing $80 million, whereas equity market inflows remained comparatively modest at $124.4 million. The benchmark six-month T-bill currently offers a return of 12.54 percent following the recent policy rate adjustment.

Financial sector experts observe that these lucrative, near-risk-free returns—bolstered by a stable exchange rate maintained for over a year—have also encouraged domestic participants using overseas accounts. However, economists warn that the heavy government borrowing through these high-yield instruments leaves limited room for the local private sector to secure commercial bank loans.

stories.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 Models Ahead of IPO
stories.summary:
Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has introduced two new systems, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as part of its strategy to strengthen its standing in the competitive AI market prior to an initial public offering. The company stated that Claude Fable 5.2 is built for programming, reasoning, and agent tasks, while Claude Mythos 5.2 targets authorized cybersecurity and life-sciences research.

Availability will vary between the two releases, with Claude Fable 5.2 offered more widely and Claude Mythos 5.2 limited strictly to organizations verified through Anthropic’s specific approval programs. According to the firm, the fresh models deliver outputs up to 30 percent quicker than the previous Claude 5.1 generation and feature improved communication clarity for users.

Pricing for the new offerings is set at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, marking a reduction compared to earlier Fable and Mythos editions. This rollout succeeds the October introduction of Claude Haiku 5.5 as the startup continuously expands its offerings.

The releases arrive amid escalating industry rivalry, where major players including OpenAI, Google under Alphabet, and Meta Platforms regularly deploy advanced models focused on reasoning, coding, and agents to capture developers and enterprise clients.

stories.title: Sardar Yaqoob Nasir Claims Shehbaz Faces Heavier Constraints Than Nawaz
stories.summary:
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz Central Senior Vice President and National Assembly member Sardar Yaqoob Nasir stated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif encounters greater operational restrictions than Nawaz Sharif experienced during his own time in office. Speaking in an exclusive interview, the PML-N leader noted that Nawaz Sharif had previously conceded he could not govern entirely according to his personal desires during his third term.

Expressing personal grievances, Nasir shared that he faced significant difficulties attempting to visit Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra, recounting instances where he waited outside the gates for three days without gaining entry. He noted that security personnel strictly prohibited meetings, leading him to ponder leaving the political party multiple times due to what he perceived as a lack of attention from leadership.

Turning to regional governance, Nasir voiced strong opposition to implementing an emergency or Governor’s Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, arguing such steps conflict with democratic principles. He noted that criminal elements have turned extortion and kidnapping into structured operations in the region.

Furthermore, Nasir disclosed that he personally receives threats and asserted that criminal networks possess extensive knowledge regarding his business operations, underscoring the severity of ongoing security challenges in the area.

stories.title: Political Economy Expert Argues Kleptocrats Stifle Pakistan Economic Progress
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s economy continues to display weak vital indicators despite broad stabilization efforts, functioning similarly to a patient discharged from intensive care but remaining hospitalized. Since 2024, per capita gross domestic product growth has hovered near zero, representing the slowest pace recorded across South Asia and threatening to push the nation toward the bottom of regional rankings.

Stalling incomes have driven extreme poverty up to 23 percent, a rate roughly ten times higher than India's, while domestic output remains heavily tilted toward consumption at 82 percent rather than investment at 14 percent. Industry's contribution to GDP has stagnated near a fifth for over five decades, falling significantly behind neighboring countries and severely constraining technology, job creation, and export expansion.

Capital scarcity remains a persistent issue as the nation neglects domestic savings and targets limited foreign capital primarily toward domestic sectors rather than export-driven areas. Exports have dropped to roughly one-tenth of GDP, while tax revenues sit near 11 percent of GDP and rely heavily on indirect levies that burden vulnerable populations, contrasted by minimal development spending compared to routine expenditures.

The author argues that these structural failures stem from deliberate choices by ruling kleptocrats who prioritize preserving their own wealth and power over enacting reforms that could foster genuine national development and democratic progress.

stories.title: Analysis Examines Structural Failures and Governance Behind Pakistan Economic Slump
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s macroeconomic indicators continue to struggle despite claims of stabilization, with per capita GDP growth remaining near zero since 2024 to register the slowest pace in South Asia. Incomes are stagnating, and extreme poverty has climbed to 23 percent, creating a stark divergence from regional peers who maintain significantly higher investment and employment rates.

The domestic economic structure relies heavily on consumption at 82 percent while keeping investment low at 14 percent, a dynamic that suppresses industrial development, which has hovered around a fifth of GDP for over fifty years. Furthermore, capital scarcity, declining export shares falling to a tenth of GDP, and low tax revenues around 11 percent of GDP leave the country dependent on external borrowing and strict international financial terms.

Heavy public debt repayment obligations consume a vast share of federal outlays, starving development initiatives and creating a continuous cycle of fiscal deficits and economic vulnerability. Remittances frequently substitute for robust export earnings, yet they primarily fuel consumption rather than establishing long-term productive capacity.

The persistent crisis is attributed not merely to administrative ineptitude, but to governance driven by political elites whose interests are served by maintaining a weak economic framework, highlighting the urgent need for genuine democratic and civilian leadership.

stories.title: فیصل آباد میں سیلز گرل پر تشدد، مریم نواز کی حمایت پر بحث
stories.summary:
پنجاب کی وزیر اعلیٰ مریم نواز نے سوشل میڈیا پر ایک ویڈیو جاری کی ہے جس میں ایک شخص کو پولیس کی تحویل میں دیکھا جا سکتا ہے۔ اس ویڈیو میں ایک خاتون کرسی پر بیٹھی ہیں جو ملزم کے کمرے میں داخل ہوتے ہی اسے تھپڑ مارنا شروع کر دیتی ہیں۔ یہ واقعہ فیصل آباد کی ایک دکان کا ہے جہاں خواتین کے زیر جامے فروخت کیے جاتے ہیں۔

واقعے کے پس منظر کے مطابق دکان کے مالک محمد رمضان کرایہ وصول کرنے کے لیے اس دکان پر آئے تھے۔ سیلز گرل نے انہیں بتایا کہ یہ خواتین کے زیر جامے کی دکان ہے اور کرائے کے لیے کاروباری مالک سے رابطہ کیا جائے۔ اس بات پر دکان کے مالک غصے میں آ گئے اور سیلز گرل پر تشدد کیا۔ پولیس کے مطابق اس واقعے کی کوئی باضابطہ درخواست یا ہیلپ لائن پر اطلاع موصول نہیں ہوئی تھی۔

تاہم، سینٹرل پولیس آفیسر کے نوٹس پر پولیس نے سی سی ٹی وی فوٹیج کی مدد سے ملزم محمد رمضان کو گرفتار کر لیا اور اس کی تصاویر بھی جاری کیں۔ مریم نواز نے اس کارروائی کو سراہتے ہوئے کہا کہ اب کوئی بھی امیر یا با اثر شخص غریب یا کمزور پر ظلم کرنے کی جرات نہیں کرے گا اور حکومت مظلوم کے ساتھ کھڑی ہوگی۔

اس اقدام پر سوشل میڈیا اور عوامی حلقوں میں ملا جلا ردِعمل سامنے آیا ہے۔ جہاں کچھ افراد نے اسے غریبوں کے ساتھ ہمدردی اور علامتی انصاف قرار دیا، وہیں ناقدین اور صحافیوں نے پولیس حراست میں ملزم کو اس طرح پیش کرنے کو قانون کی حکمرانی کے خلاف اور ماورائے عدالت عمل قرار دیا۔ ناقدین کا کہنا ہے کہ اس طرح کے اقدامات سے معاشرہ لاقانونیت کی طرف جا سکتا ہے۔

اس سے قبل بھی مریم نواز نے لاہور میں پیٹرول پمپ ملازم پر تشدد اور ایک لڑکی پر تشدد کے واقعات میں ملزمان کی زیرِ حراست ویڈیوز شیئر کی تھیں اور متاثرین کی جانب سے ردِعمل کی حمایت کی تھی۔ وفاقی وزیرِ اطلاعات عطا اللہ تارڑ نے اس حوالے سے مؤقف اختیار کیا کہ وزیرِ اعلیٰ نے ایک ماں اور بہن کے طور پر انسانی جذبات کے تحت مظلوم کا ساتھ دیا ہے۔

stories.title: China Rejects Claims Linking Nvidia CEO Controversy to Espionage
stories.summary:
China’s Foreign Ministry has dismissed recent media claims connecting a personal controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to Chinese intelligence operations. During a regular press briefing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun labeled the allegations as unfounded, politically motivated smears designed to malign China's reputation without credible evidence.

The response follows statements by US President Donald Trump, who mentioned that the FBI is examining an affair between Huang and a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Trump noted he was amazed by the situation, stated that Huang claimed ignorance of the woman's background, and expressed belief that the CEO would remain in good shape despite the unfolding controversy.

Nvidia shares experienced a decline of over four percent after the company's board initiated an internal investigation to determine if Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence efforts. The probe brings significant attention to the 63-year-old CEO, who serves as a prominent figure in the artificial intelligence boom and holds a major stake in the world's most valuable chipmaker.

Meanwhile, the controversy has sparked broader reactions, including proposed class-action litigation from shareholders accusing Huang and Nvidia of concealing ties to the suspected intelligence asset. Lawmakers in the United States have also indicated that the situation may prompt stricter congressional measures regarding China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.

stories.title: کراچی: لیاقت آباد میں بچی سے جنسی ہراسانی پر ملزم کو سزا
stories.summary:
ایڈیشنل ڈسٹرکٹ اینڈ سیشن عدالت وسطی کراچی نے لیاقت آباد کے علاقے میں ایک کم عمر بچی کو جنسی طور پر ہراسانی کا نشانہ بنانے کا جرم ثابت ہونے پر ملزم کو چودہ سال قید کی سزا سنا دی ہے۔ عدالت کی جانب سے مجرم پر دس لاکھ روپے جرمانہ بھی عائد کیا گیا ہے۔

مقدمے کے فیصلے میں عدالت نے واضح کیا کہ متاثرہ لڑکی کی طرف سے ٹرائل کے دوران ملزم کو معافی دینے کا بیان دیا گیا تھا، تاہم جنسی استحصال جیسے سنگین جرم میں یہ معافی ملزم کی بریت کی بنیاد نہیں بن سکتی۔ عدالت نے یہ بھی کہا کہ تفتیش کی کسی بھی خامی کی بنا پر ملزم کو بری نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔

پراسیکیوشن کے مطابق اس واقعے کا مقدمہ سال 2023ء میں لیاقت آباد کے تھانے میں درج کیا گیا تھا۔ اس معاملے کی سماعت کے دوران تفتیشی افسر نے مفرور ملزمان سے متعلق رپورٹ بھی عدالت میں پیش کی تھی۔

عدالت کا یہ فیصلہ بچوں کے خلاف ہونے والے جرائم کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی اور انصاف کی فراہمی کے تناظر میں انتہائی اہمیت کا حامل ہے۔ اس سے معاشرے میں ایسے سنگین جرائم کے مرتکب افراد کے لیے عبرت کا پیغام ملتا ہے اور قانون کی عملداری یقینی بنتی ہے۔

stories.title: کراچی: منشیات برآمدگی کیس میں شریک ملزمہ نسیم بی بی مفرور قرار
stories.summary:
کراچی کی انسدادِ منشیات کی عدالت میں منشیات برآمدگی کے ایک مقدمے کی سماعت ہوئی جس میں مرکزی ملزمہ انمول عرف پنکی کو جیل حکام کی جانب سے ویڈیو لنک کے ذریعے عدالت میں پیش کیا گیا۔ سماعت کے دوران تفتیشی افسر نے مفرور ملزمان کے حوالے سے تفصیلی رپورٹ عدالت میں جمع کروائی۔

تفتیشی افسر نے عدالت کو آگاہ کیا کہ اس مقدمے کی شریک ملزمہ نسیم بی بی کا تاحال کوئی سراغ نہیں مل سکا ہے۔ اس رپورٹ کے بعد عدالت نے نسیم بی بی کو باضابطہ طور پر مفرور قرار دے دیا اور ساتھ ہی نسیم بی بی اور جاوید کو اشتہاری قرار دینے کی قانونی کارروائی شروع کرنے کی ہدایت جاری کی۔

عدالت نے یہ بھی حکم دیا کہ ملزمان سے متعلق اشتہارات شائع کروائے جائیں۔ اس کے علاوہ ملزمہ کو مقدمے کی نقول فراہم کرنے کے لیے 24 نومبر کی تاریخ مقرر کی گئی ہے، اور عدالت کا کہنا ہے کہ نقول کی فراہمی کے بعد ملزمہ پر باضابطہ طور پر فردِ جرم عائد کی جائے گی۔

مزید برآں، اینٹی نارکوٹکس فورس (اے این ایف) نے اینٹی منی لانڈرنگ ایکٹ کے تحت ملزمہ کے اثاثے ضبط کرنے کی درخواست بھی دائر کر رکھی ہے، جس پر عدالت نے آئندہ سماعت میں فریقین سے دلائل طلب کیے ہیں۔ یہ کیس منشیات کے خلاف جاری قانونی کارروائیوں کا ایک اہم حصہ ہے۔

stories.title: حکومت اور جماعتِ اسلامی کے مذاکرات کا فائنل راؤنڈ آج ہو گا
stories.summary:
جماعتِ اسلامی کے نائب امیر لیاقت بلوچ نے اپنے ایک بیان میں اعلان کیا ہے کہ حکومت اور جماعتِ اسلامی کی سب کمیٹی کے درمیان مذاکرات کا آج آخری اور فیصلہ کن راؤنڈ منعقد ہوگا۔ یہ اجلاس وزارتِ خارجہ کے کمیٹی روم میں ڈپٹی وزیرِ اعظم اسحاق ڈار کی میزبانی میں ہوگا۔

لیاقت بلوچ نے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ حکومت کو پیٹرولیم لیوی کم کرنی چاہیے اور عوام کو ریلیف فراہم کرنے کے لیے فوری اقدامات کرنے چاہئیں کیونکہ تیل، بجلی اور گیس کی بلند قیمتیں اور بھاری ٹیکسوں کا بوجھ اب عوام کے لیے بالکل ناقابل برداشت بن چکا ہے۔ انہوں نے حکومت کی طرف سے سیلاب متاثرین کے لیے اعلان کردہ ریلیف کو اونٹ کے منہ میں زیرے کے مترادف قرار دیا۔

رہنما جماعتِ اسلامی کا کہنا تھا کہ سرکاری محکموں میں پھیلی ہوئی کرپشن کا کینسر ملکی معیشت کے لیے ایک بہت بڑا روگ ہے۔ انہوں نے اس بات کا اعادہ کیا کہ تیل پر لیوی میں کمی اور گیس کی درآمد کے حوالے سے مافیا کا خاتمہ کرنے سے ہی معیشت کا پہیہ دوبارہ تیزی سے رواں دواں ہو سکتا ہے۔

انہوں نے امید ظاہر کی کہ جماعتِ اسلامی کی جانب سے عوام کو مہنگائی اور مسائل سے ریلیف دلانے کی یہ مسلسل جدوجہد ضرور رنگ لائے گی اور مذاکرات میں مثبت پیش رفت متوقع ہے۔

stories.title: Trump Confirms FBI Investigation Into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary:
United States President Donald Trump stated that the FBI is examining an affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a Beijing intelligence asset. Trump expressed surprise over the allegations against Huang, whom he considers a close ally in Silicon Valley, and noted that the CEO claimed he was unaware of the woman's background.

The development follows an announcement by Nvidia's board regarding an internal investigation into whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Nvidia shares dropped more than four percent following the news, putting a spotlight on the 63-year-old executive as the prominent figure driving the global artificial intelligence boom.

In response to the reports, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun strongly rejected the accusations, calling the narrative a groundless and slanderous smear campaign. Concurrently, Nvidia shareholders filed a proposed class-action lawsuit accusing leadership of concealing ties to the suspected spy, while lawmakers urged tighter legislative restrictions on AI chip sales to China.

The situation involves Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. While Nvidia's board maintains confidence in the CEO, analysts note that the unfolding situation has introduced uncertainty regarding corporate leadership and succession planning.

stories.title: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Faces Impeachment Vote This Week
stories.summary:
Representative Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, initiating a procedure that leads to a scheduled House vote on Wednesday. The charges against Hegseth include waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power, drawing comparisons to William Belknap, the sole civilian leader of the US military previously impeached in 1876.

Congressional sources indicate the resolution might secure the simple majority required to pass the Republican-controlled House before Democrats assume control on January 3. However, a conviction in the Senate remains unlikely, as it demands a two-thirds majority where Republicans hold 53 seats. House Speaker Mike Johnson opposed the impeachment effort, citing negative implications for international allies and adversaries during ongoing hostilities.

Hegseth has strongly defended his position, running a social media campaign insisting he will not step down and drawing parallels to President Donald Trump's prior impeachments. Trump has publicly backed Hegseth and condemned the impeachment push, pointing to military actions in Iran and the removal of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

The political battle highlights deep divisions within the Republican party regarding conflicts abroad. Voter frustration concerning the war played a role in Democrats capturing control of Congress in recent midterm elections, further intensifying the debate over military engagements.

stories.title: Jemima Goldsmith Accuses Russell Brand of Abuse Following Prison Sentence
stories.summary:
Jemima Goldsmith has publicly accused her former boyfriend, Russell Brand, of violence, coercive control, and abuse during their approximately one-year relationship around 2014. Goldsmith revealed that she once called the police to have Brand removed from her home following a violent incident in 2014, though she chose not to press charges at the time to protect her teenage children from media attention.

The allegations surfaced via social media on Monday, shortly after Brand was sentenced to ten-and-a-half years in prison for rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women between 2004 and 2009. Goldsmith expressed relief that Brand had finally faced justice and stated she would have been willing to testify during investigations if journalists faced legal action.

Her statement also addressed a 2015 injunction involving a woman named Szilvia Berki, who visited Goldsmith's home in June 2014 to provide Brand a massage. Goldsmith stated that the arrangement was canceled upon her arrival and that police found no case to answer after reviewing her statement and CCTV footage regarding Berki's subsequent claims that Brand pushed her.

Goldsmith further claimed that Berki sent threatening and antisemitic messages following the incident. She noted that recent media coverage surrounding the injunction has subjected her to online abuse, prompting her to share her personal experience regarding Brand's behavior.

stories.title: NCCIA Recovers Rs3.2 Million in Scams and Arrests Child Exploiter
stories.summary:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency launched a crackdown in Rawalpindi, recovering Rs3.2 million across two online fraud cases while arresting a suspect for child exploitation and blackmailing. In the first case, officials recovered Rs1.8 million after a citizen lost over Rs2.9 million through a Facebook and WhatsApp investment scam involving a fraudulent mobile application named “Onchainus.net”. 

In the second case, a Rawalpindi resident named Muhammad Arshad, son of Ameer Khan, was defrauded of more. than Rs21 million through an online trading scheme via a WhatsApp group called “v185-Wharton”. The agency recovered Rs1.4 million from this operation, and the accused individual remains in physical remand while investigations continue to track down other network members. 

Separately, the NCCIA apprehended a suspect following a complaint by Mushtaq Khan, who reported that his son was targeted during online gaming. The accused allegedly lured the minor to his home under the guise of providing a gaming ID, exploited him, and recorded videos to blackmail him. Authorities seized a mobile phone from the suspect and initiated a forensic analysis of the digital evidence.

In addition to these actions, the agency issued a public warning regarding fake messages circulating about a Rs13,000 cash prize from the prime minister. Officials cautioned citizens that unverified links could compromise personal and banking information. The public is urged to report cybercrime incidents to helpline 1799 or at the nearest NCCIA circle as authorities continue their zero-tolerance policy.

stories.title: Chaudhry Hussain Elahi Slams Punjab CM Over Development Bias
stories.summary:
Political tensions among the Chaudhrys of Gujrat resurfaced after PML-Q MNA Chaudhry Hussain Elahi criticized Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for allegedly blocking development funds and showing a discriminatory approach. Speaking at a public gathering near Tanda, Hussain Elahi accused the provincial administration of halting uplift schemes initiated during the tenure of former CM Chaudhry Parvez Elahi in 2022. He claimed the government spent Rs11 billion on a plane for the chief minister while failing to release Rs3 billion needed to complete public welfare projects in his constituency.

The verbal clash follows earlier remarks by federal minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain praising Parvez Elahi, which prompted CM Maryam to issue a legal notice and challenge him to prove allegations of corruption. Responding to the legal threats, Hussain Elahi stated that the people of Gujrat are not afraid of courts and threatened to drag the entire Punjab government into legal proceedings. He also alleged corruption in provincial projects such as Suthra Punjab and Model Village, a sentiment echoed by his father, Chaudhry Wajahat Hussain.

Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari dismissed the criticism, stating that the administration's development initiatives are causing discomfort among certain political elements who failed to improve Gujrat despite holding office for years. Meanwhile, familial divisions were highlighted when PTI-aligned leader Moonis Elahi dispelled rumors of a family reunion. He criticized Wajahat's camp, stating that their complaints stem from failing to secure ministerial portfolios like their cousins.

The ongoing war of words underscores deep-seated political and personal rifts within the family, splitting allegiances between different factions of the PML-Q and the coalition government.

stories.title: اینویڈیا کے سربراہ جینسن ہوانگ اور مبینہ چینی جاسوس کے تعلقات کی تحقیقات
stories.summary:
امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے تصدیق کی ہے کہ ایف بی آئی اینویڈیا کے چیف ایگزیکٹو جینسن ہوانگ اور ایک مبینہ چینی کاروباری خاتون اور جاسوس ایلس ہوانگ کے درمیان تعلقات کی تحقیقات کر रही ہے۔ ٹرمپ نے بتایا کہ انہوں نے جینسن ہوانگ سے بات کی تھی جنہوں نے اس بات سے لاعلمی کا اظہار کیا کہ ایلس ہوانگ ایک جاسوس تھیں۔

نیویارک ٹائمز کی رپورٹ کے مطابق، امریکی انٹیلی جنس حکام کا ماننا ہے کہ سنگاپور کی کمپنی میگا سپیড سے وابستہ ایلس ہوانگ بیجنگ کے لیے جاسوسی کر रही थीं। इस खुलासे के बाद निवेशकों की चिंता बढ़ गई और सोमवार को एनवीडिया के शेयरों में चार प्रतिशत से अधिक की गिरावट आई जिससे कंपनी के बाजार मूल्य में लगभग 250 अरब डॉलर की कमी दर्ज की गई।

एनवीडिया के बोर्ड ऑफ डायरेक्टर्स ने इन खबरों के मद्देनजर एक स्वतंत्र जांच शुरू कर दी है, हालांकि कंपनी का कहना है कि उनके पास इस बात का कोई प्रमाण नहीं है कि इससे राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा या कंपनी के गोपनीय राज प्रभावित हुए हैं। बोर्ड ने स्पष्ट किया कि अमेरिकी राष्ट्रीय और आर्थिक सुरक्षा उनकी सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता है।

दूसरी ओर, जेनسن ہوانگ نے اپنے ایک الگ ذاتی بیان میں اپنی اہلیہ سے بے وفائی کا اعتراف کرتے ہوئے اپنے خاندان، ملازمین اور حصص یافتگان سے معافی مانگی ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ وہ اس معاملے کی مکمل ذمہ داری قبول کرتے ہیں और बोर्ड की जांच में पूरा सहयोग करेंगे। बीजिंग ने इन सभी जासूसी के आरोपों को निराधार और चीन को बदनाम करने की साजिश करार दिया है।

stories.title: Cricket Australia Rules Out Reopening 2018 Sandpapergate Investigation
stories.summary:
Cricket Australia Chief Executive Todd Greenberg has dismissed calls to reopen the investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, despite fresh claims from Usman Khawaja and David Warner that knowledge of the plot was widespread across the team. Greenberg stated on a local radio station that Khawaja's autobiography contained details contradicting previous statements, but emphasized that the governing body remains comfortable with the original investigation's outcome and sees no reason to revisit the matter.

The scandal initially erupted during the Cape Town Test in 2018, leading Cricket Australia to impose bans and penalties on Steve Smith, David Warner, and Cameron Bancroft. In his newly released book, Khawaja asserts that open discussions about altering the ball with sandpaper involved players across the entire team rather than just a select few. Warner, who retired from international cricket over two years ago, publicly backed Khawaja's claims, describing the original governing body probe as rushed and botched.

Former CA CEO James Sutherland declined to comment, while Bancroft has not addressed the recent remarks directly, though he previously stated that teammates besides Smith and Warner were aware of the plan. Four Australian bowlers who played in the 2018 match—Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, and Nathan Lyon—previously issued a joint statement denying any knowledge of the scheme. Current Test captain Cummins noted that he had discussed the book with Khawaja and expressed no concern regarding potential fallout.

Some commentators have questioned the timing of Khawaja's revelations, suggesting commercial motives for his book release. Khawaja refuted these claims on social media, maintaining that financial gain was not a factor in his decision to share his account.

stories.title: Cricket Scotland Suspends Bilateral Matches Against Afghanistan Over Women's Rights
stories.summary:
Cricket Scotland announced it will no longer schedule bilateral cricket matches against Afghanistan outside of International Cricket Council events, citing human rights concerns and the treatment of women under the Taliban government. The governing body stated that its decision supports growing women's and girls' participation in the sport and aligns with similar suspensions enacted by Cricket Australia and the England and Wales Cricket Board.

Since returning to power in 2021, the Taliban government has effectively erased women's sports and severely restricted access to education and employment for women and girls in Afghanistan. While the Taliban maintains that its policies comply with Islamic law and local customs, international sporting bodies continue to face pressure over Afghanistan's membership status.

Cricket Scotland noted that its new policy will be reviewed annually or following major ICC decisions and changing circumstances. Although Scotland has not played Afghanistan in a full international match since the 2021 T20 World Cup, the Afghanistan Cricket Board recently requested training facilities in Scotland for upcoming series and leagues.

Addressing contractual obligations, Cricket Scotland stated it will consider issuing no-objection certificates if the ICC officially approves the Afghan league. However, the organization emphasized that issuing an NOC does not constitute an endorsement of the current Afghan regime or its policies.

stories.title: David Warner Backs Khawaja's Claims on 2018 Ball-Tampering Scandal
stories.summary:
Former Australian cricketer David Warner stated that teammate Usman Khawaja's account regarding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa is completely accurate. In an excerpt from his autobiography, Khawaja claimed that discussions about tampering with the ball using sandpaper during the Newlands Test in Cape Town were widespread throughout the entire team rather than isolated to a few individuals.

Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, received bans following the 2018 incident. In an Instagram video, Warner voiced his support for Khawaja and criticized Cricket Australia's original probe as flawed and rushed. He pointed out that investigators failed to interview Khawaja despite him sitting next to Bancroft during the tour, raising questions about the thoroughness of the inquiry.

Emphasizing a demand for accountability and transparency rather than old grievances, Warner stated that the focus should shift toward those responsible for the investigation. He noted that numerous inaccuracies and statements had circulated in the media over the past eight years while many individuals remained silent. 

Cricket Australia defended its 2018 findings in a recent statement, maintaining that all relevant information was properly considered and that prior knowledge of the plot was restricted to Smith, Warner, and Bancroft. Meanwhile, Australian Test captain Pat Cummins, one of four bowlers from the 2018 match who denied prior knowledge of the scheme in a 2018 joint statement, dismissed concerns about potential fallout from Khawaja's book release following discussions with his teammate.

stories.title: Mitchell Starc Denies Knowledge of 2018 Ball-Tampering Scandal
stories.summary:
Fast bowler Mitchell Starc has publicly denied any prior knowledge of Australia's ball-tampering plot during their 2018 tour of South Africa. Speaking to reporters in Sydney on Tuesday, Starc maintained that his recollection and position had not changed from a 2021 statement issued by the bowlers, asserting they were unaware a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the ball. Starc is the first Australian bowler to respond to recent claims made by Usman Khawaja in his autobiography and on social media, where Khawaja asserted that the entire team knew about a plan to manipulate the ball to achieve reverse swing, beginning at the second test in Gqeberha.

The controversy intensified when former test opening batsman David Warner broke his silence on Monday, endorsing Khawaja's account as entirely accurate and criticizing the original Cricket Australia investigation as rushed and botched. The 2018 incident during the Cape Town test previously resulted in bans and penalties for then-captain Steve Smith, Warner, and Cameron Bancroft. Despite growing demands from media pundits and former players like Michael Clarke to reopen the investigation, Cricket Australia boss Todd Greenberg stated on Tuesday that there was no compelling reason to do so, noting that player accounts contradict Khawaja's version and that the governing body remains comfortable with the original outcome.

Other key figures involved in the 2018 series have largely declined to comment or maintained their previous stances. Former Cricket Australia CEO James Sutherland chose not to comment, while Bancroft declined to speak with Australian media after previously suggesting in 2021 that teammates besides Smith and Warner were aware of the plan. Meanwhile, current captain Pat Cummins stated last month that the issue had already been thoroughly addressed and dealt with years ago.

While some commentators have questioned the timing of Khawaja's revelations and accused him of attempting to boost book sales, Khawaja rejected any commercial motives on social media, stating he does not need the money. The ongoing dispute continues to divide opinions within Australian cricket regarding the exact timeline and level of awareness surrounding the Sandpapergate scandal.

stories.title: Debate Over Creating New Administrative Provinces Gains Momentum in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Discussions surrounding the creation of new administrative units and provinces in Pakistan have resurfaced, supported by coalition partner figures including Defence Minister Khawaja Asif. Asif suggested the country could establish up to 12 new provinces if decisions were based purely on administrative necessity rather than ethnic, linguistic, or political factors. Redrawing boundaries, however, consistently carries significant political and ethnic implications.

Recent speculation points toward a potential 28th constitutional amendment to facilitate restructuring, with implementation possibly deferred until after the next general election due to complex legal and resource challenges. Critics argue that pushing legislation through the current parliament lacks national consensus, especially given lingering public doubts stemming from the Election Commission's conduct during the 2024 general election.

Instead of redrawing provincial boundaries, analysts suggest empowering local government systems to address service delivery failures and population pressures effectively. Successive civilian administrations have often concentrated power in provincial centers rather than operationalizing local governance tiers designed to ensure allocated resources reach citizens directly.

Political leadership faces a choice between pursuing constitutional restructuring or strengthening local governance structures to manage internal migration and resource distribution. Observers recommend prioritizing electoral reforms with the opposition to restore public trust before undertaking any major constitutional changes.

stories.title: Lahore Qalandars Appoint Aminul Islam as High-Performance Advisor
stories.summary:
Pakistan Super League franchise Lahore Qalandars announced on Tuesday the appointment of former Bangladesh cricket captain Aminul Islam as an advisor to the team's High-Performance Centres. In his new role, Islam will guide the development of these centres with a primary focus on enhancing player development, refining coaching practices, and establishing structured pathways for young cricketers to advance in the sport. This strategic move aims to reinforce the franchise's grassroots cricket initiatives while expanding its presence and outreach in Bangladesh by leveraging Islam's extensive background in both international play and cricket administration.

Islam brings decades of administrative and leadership experience to the Lahore Qalandars franchise. He previously served as the International Cricket Council's Cricket Development Manager for Asia from 2015 to 2025 and also worked as a Cricket Development Officer for the Asian Cricket Council. Additionally, his administrative background includes serving as president of the Bangladesh Cricket Board. As a player, Islam represented the national team of Bangladesh from 1988 to 2002 and captained the side during the 1999 Cricket World Cup.

The appointment aligns with Lahore Qalandars' established reputation for discovering and nurturing emerging athletic talent through dedicated grassroots and high-performance programs. By incorporating Islam's wealth of international experience, the franchise seeks to further strengthen the operational success of these development frameworks. The initiative highlights the team's ongoing commitment to investing in youth development infrastructure and regional sports collaboration.

stories.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Two Houthi Missiles Targeted at Riyadh
stories.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement directed two missiles toward the Saudi capital of Riyadh, which were successfully intercepted and destroyed by the Saudi-led coalition. Air defenses neutralized both a ballistic missile and a cruise missile during the incident, following early-warning alerts issued by Saudi Civil Defence.

In a separate operation, the coalition also targeted and destroyed a ballistic missile heading toward Saudi Arabia's southern region. This triggered prior warning alerts in the southwestern cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait before authorities confirmed that the threats had cleared.

The region bordering Yemen has faced frequent missile and drone strikes targeting local military installations and energy infrastructure. These attacks have intensified alongside a broader conflict involving the US, Israel, and Iran.

The escalation follows a Houthi advance in September toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital shipping chokepoint situated at the southern entrance of the Red Sea. Meanwhile, the coalition has continued conducting retaliatory airstrikes against Houthi positions within Yemen.

stories.title: Migrant Boat Sinking Off Senegal Death Toll Climbs to 39
stories.summary:
Local authorities in Senegal confirmed on Monday that the death toll from a recent migrant shipwreck off the country's northwest coast has risen to 39. The disaster marks one of the deadliest maritime migration incidents in the region in recent years, involving a wooden pirogue that broke into two pieces on a deserted stretch of shoreline in Thieppe village.

Louga regional Governor Ndeye Nguenar Mbodj raised the casualty count by four on Monday morning after search teams recovered four additional bodies in an advanced state of decomposition. Officials requested authorization to bury the latest victims on-site. The deceased were primarily local residents hailing from nearby communities such as Thieppe and Potou, who had attempted to join the perilous sea route toward Spain's Canary Islands.

In a parallel operation on Friday, Senegalese police intercepted 142 individuals aboard another small vessel attempting the same journey toward Europe. That group included 23 women, two babies, and two children originating from Senegal, The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, and Nigeria. The interception coincides with a severe surge in maritime arrivals reported by Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro.

Since the beginning of November, officials on El Hierro declared an emergency after recording more than 3,300 migrant arrivals transported across roughly 30 separate boats. The ongoing crisis highlights the persistent dangers faced by west African migrants attempting unauthorized sea crossings in search of better opportunities.

stories.title: US Dollar Holds Firm as Traders Await Inflation Figures
stories.summary:
During Tuesday's Asian trading session, the US dollar remained stable as market participants braced for upcoming US inflation data. Strong recent employment figures have already elevated expectations for potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

The Australian and New Zealand dollars both posted gains, while the euro recovered from a previous decline. Market sentiment has shifted from anticipating interest rate cuts to pricing in hikes, largely driven by energy price increases stemming from the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

Analysts note that higher-than-expected Consumer Price Index figures could further solidify expectations for a December rate increase. A recent October jobs report indicated hiring levels more than double initial forecasts, leading markets to price in an 84 percent probability of a near-term hike.

Meanwhile, Japan's yen hovered around 157.97 per dollar, supported by previous heavy official intervention that included selling $97 billion in reserves. The ongoing threat of additional currency interventions has helped maintain the yen's stability despite fading expectations for a domestic rate increase.

stories.title: Chancellor Friedrich Merz Nominates Ilse Aigner as Germany's First Female President
stories.summary:
Germany is on track to appoint its first female head of state next year following a nomination announced in Berlin on Monday. Chancellor Friedrich Merz put forward Ilse Aigner as the joint conservative candidate to succeed current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose term concludes in March.

Aigner is heavily favored to win the January election within the Federal Convention, which consists of members from the lower house of parliament and delegates representing Germany's 16 federal state parliaments. Her candidacy has secured backing from Merz's conservative bloc, their coalition partners the Social Democrats, and the Green party, bridging several political divides.

Addressing the public alongside Chancellor Merz, Aigner emphasized her commitment to combating societal division if elected to the largely ceremonial post. She warned that the country's democracy faces internal and external threats from rising ideologies, extremism, and the systematic disparagement of national consensus.

Although Aigner did not specify particular political movements during her remarks, mainstream German parties continue to navigate the growing influence of the far-right Alternative for Germany party. Recent opinion polls suggest that the far-right group could emerge as the largest political force following the federal elections scheduled for early 2029.

stories.title: Mauricio Pochettino Emerges as Top Candidate for Manchester United
stories.summary:
United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the leading candidate to take over as the next manager of Manchester United, according to reports. The Red Devils are reportedly weighing the dismissal of current manager Michael Carrick following a dismal start to the Premier League season. The team recently slipped to 18th place in the league table after a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, leaving them winless with three losses and five draws since August 30. Securing only one victory and accumulating eight points through 10 matches, the club is currently enduring its worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign.

Pochettino, who is 54 years old, possesses extensive managerial experience in English football and Europe, having previously coached Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea, and Paris Saint-Germain before taking charge of the USMNT in 2024. Following a successful run leading the United States to the round of 16 at the World Cup, the Argentine manager signed a contract extension in August that ties him to the national team until 2030. Despite this commitment, speculation surrounds his potential return to club management at Old Trafford.

In addition to Pochettino, Manchester United's leadership hierarchy is evaluating several alternative candidates for the managerial position. These reportedly include former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe, former Ipswich Town coach Kieran McKenna, and former German national team coach Julian Nagelsmann. Nagelsmann recently became available after resigning following Germany's elimination in the round of 32 at the World Cup in July.

Manchester United faces a crucial stretch ahead as they prepare for their next fixture away at Liverpool on November 22. The upcoming match follows a brief international break that gives the club's management time to evaluate their options regarding the future of the managerial position amidst ongoing league struggles.

stories.title: Asian Stocks Rally as Declining Oil Prices Ease Market Worries
stories.summary:
Stock markets across Asia experienced notable gains as crude oil prices retreated. Investors responded to remarks from US President Donald Trump regarding a pause in potential military strikes against Iran, alleviating some global economic anxiety ahead of key inflation reports.

Benchmark oil prices dropped significantly, trading well below $100 per barrel and reaching their lowest levels since early September. This slump helped soothe inflation fears following a previous market downturn that was exacerbated by US midterm election outcomes and regulatory concerns surrounding the technology sector.

Regional indexes responded positively, with South Korea's KOSPI rising over 5 percent and Japan's Nikkei gaining roughly 3 percent in early trade. Major US indices also recorded strong gains during the previous session, reflecting a broader market rebound from recent lows.

Attention now shifts to upcoming US consumer price data, which economists expect will show continued inflation pressures. These figures are anticipated to influence the Federal Reserve's next policy decisions, with traders factoring in a strong likelihood of an interest rate increase at the next meeting.

stories.title: Netanyahu Pushes Trump Daily for Renewed War Despite Regional Alarms
stories.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly been calling US President Donald Trump daily to pressure him into resuming military action against Iran, despite ongoing diplomatic initiatives aimed at resolving the conflict. According to reports from the Financial Times, individuals briefed on the discussions indicate that Netanyahu is aggressively lobbying for a return to hostilities to force the collapse of the Iranian government, while White House officials and regional leaders actively work to counter this push and prioritize negotiations. Arab and Muslim leaders have expressed deep alarm over Netanyahu's persistent efforts, fearing that renewed fighting could trigger severe regional instability and a broader Iranian response.

During recent meetings with international leaders, including Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Nahyan, President Trump stated that Gulf allies such as Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Kuwait prefer maintaining the status quo rather than entering a new military campaign. Trump noted that there is positive momentum toward concluding the nearly nine-month war, making new US strikes appear unlikely. Concurrently, regional leaders including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and Qatari Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Nahyan have communicated with Trump to advocate for giving diplomacy more time.

Diplomatic efforts to bridge the gap between Washington and Tehran continue to face challenges. While mediators have discussed an interim agreement based on a seven-day proposal originally presented by Iran in September, Tehran maintains a rigid stance. An Iranian official recently dismissed rumors regarding talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for frozen assets, reiterating that Iran will only negotiate within the framework of seven strict conditions, which include lifting the naval blockade and unilateral sanctions, releasing frozen funds, and formally ending the war.

Hurting from stalled diplomacy, the underlying conflict reignited after a memorandum of understanding reached in July broke down. The US and Israel initially launched attacks on Iran on February 28, and while current diplomatic channels led by mediators have shown signs of progress in narrowing differences, the persistent pressure from Israel's caretaker prime minister continues to complicate the path toward a lasting settlement in the Middle East.

stories.title: Oil Prices Decline Following Trump's Remarks on Iran Escalation
stories.summary:
Crude oil futures extended previous losses after US President Donald Trump stated that immediate military action against Iran is currently unnecessary. This perspective reduced immediate worries regarding potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Both Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate futures saw downward movement, following a sharp decline in the prior session. Trump indicated a willingness to delay new military strikes following discussions with regional leaders, including Qatar's prime minister, though a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz remains in place.

Despite ongoing security incidents involving shipping lanes near the Strait of Hormuz, analysts noted that the market has not priced in extreme risk premiums due to the administration's more measured tone. Nevertheless, senior officials from the US and Gulf nations remain skeptical about the prospect of a formal peace agreement anytime soon.

On the production front, an industry survey revealed that OPEC oil output increased in October, driven by higher production volumes from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq. In a separate geopolitical development, Russian and Ukrainian representatives prepared to convene for US-brokered talks.

stories.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth Faces Impeachment Vote This Week
stories.summary:
Representative Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, introduced articles of impeachment against US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday in Washington. This legislative action initiated a strict two-day window leading up to an anticipated House vote on Wednesday, which addresses allegations including abuse of power and waging war against Iran without formal congressional approval. Hegseth, who frequently styles himself as the "secretary of war" as part of a broader effort to reform a military he initially deemed too weak and "woke" after taking office last year, could parallel William Belknap. Belknap, who held the identical title in 1876, remains the sole civilian leader of the United States military ever impeached by Congress.

Congressional insiders indicate that the impeachment resolution might secure the simple majority required to pass the Republican-controlled House prior to Democrats assuming control on January 3. Conversely, a conviction within the Senate remains highly improbable, as a two-thirds majority is mandatory and Republicans currently command 53 out of 100 seats. House Speaker Mike Johnson openly opposed the initiative, noting that pursuing impeachment amid active hostilities sends a detrimental signal to both allies and adversaries alike. Voter frustration stemming from the ongoing conflict contributed to Democratic gains in last week's midterm elections, thereby exacerbating internal Republican divisions over a war publicly questioned by Vice President J.D. Vance but staunchly defended by Hegseth as historic and courageous.

In historical precedent, William Belknap resigned and wept before his scheduled 1876 vote amidst kickback allegations, though the House proceeded with his impeachment regardless, and the Senate ultimately acquitted him due to a lack of a two-thirds threshold. In stark contrast, Hegseth has rejected resignation, launching a defiant social media campaign and asserting that efforts to oust him will fail just like the two historic impeachments faced by President Donald Trump. While Trump condemned the impeachment push during a Sunday CBS broadcast as highly unfair and praised the outcomes of recent military actions involving Iran and Venezuela, Hegseth scheduled his first Pentagon press briefing since May to address the ongoing controversy.

stories.title: Israeli Forces Kill Palestinian Teen and Wound Three in West Bank
stories.summary:
Israeli troops killed a 14-year-old Palestinian boy, Moataz Iyad Daghlas, and wounded three other individuals during a late Monday raid in Burqa, located northwest of Nablus in the occupied West Bank. According to the Palestinian Health Ministry, the General Authority of Civil Affairs notified them of the fatal shooting, which local sources reported involved live ammunition fired by soldiers who also blocked the village's main road.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society stated that Israeli forces obstructed its ambulance crews from reaching a wounded person and detained three volunteer medics responding to the village clashes. Earlier in the evening, Red Crescent teams transported a young man to the hospital with gunshot wounds to his abdomen and pelvis, while the Palestinian Medical Relief Society transferred another young man who was shot in the hand.

Simultaneously, an Al Jazeera investigation broadcast on Monday revealed that Israeli soldiers wearing civilian clothing have participated in armed attacks alongside occupier groups against Palestinians in the West Bank. The report documented 14 Palestinian deaths caused by individuals found to be active-duty military personnel or wearing army uniforms, focusing on the army’s Hagmar regional defence units whose reservist ranks have grown sixfold since 2023.

This incident occurs amid an intensification of Israeli army raids and settler attacks across the West Bank and East Jerusalem since October 2023. The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission recorded 12,506 attacks between October 2023 and June 2026, leading to 52 Palestinian deaths and 890 fires on local property and farmland.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Rebounds Strongly After Long Weekend Holiday
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a powerful rally on Tuesday as investors returned from a long weekend, pushing the benchmark KSE-100 Index up by over 5,400 points. Trading had been suspended on Monday for Iqbal Day, but the resumption brought renewed buying interest supported by strong remittance inflows and declining international oil prices.

The benchmark index settled at 179,335.24 points, marking an increase of 5,448.56 points or 3.13% from its previous close of 173,886.68. Throughout the session, the index reached an intraday high of 179,424.04 and a low of 176,273.72, reclaiming the 175,000 level for the first time since September 1, 2026.

Domestic and international factors both contributed to the positive sentiment. Strong remittance inflows reinforced confidence in the country's external account, while falling global crude prices alleviated concerns regarding imported energy costs and inflation. Internationally, Brent crude and WTI futures dropped significantly after United States President Donald Trump downplayed the necessity for further military action against Iran, easing fears of sustained regional supply disruptions.

Major contributors to the rally included UBL, LUCK, MEBL, SYS, ENGROH, BAHL, HBL, HUBC, OGDC, and PPL, which collectively added around 1,981 points. Total trading volume reached 972.4 million shares with a traded value of Rs50.6 billion across 501 companies, of which 363 stocks advanced.

stories.title: شیخ حسینہ کی پاسپورٹ کے لیے درخواست: بنگلہ دیش اور بھارت میں سفارتی تناؤ
stories.summary:
بنگلہ دیش کی معزول وزیر اعظم شیخ حسینہ واجد نے بھارت میں خود ساختہ جلاوطنی کے دوران وطن واپس آنے کے لیے ایک نئے پاسپورٹ اور قومی شناختی کارڈ کے اجراء کی باضابطہ درخواست جمع کرا دی ہے۔ یہ درخواست لندن کی میٹرکس چیمبرس لا فرم کے ایک وکیل کے توسط سے نئی دہلی میں واقع بنگلہ دیشی ہائی کمیشن میں دائر کی گئی ہے۔ ہائی کمیشن نے اس درخواست کو موصول کرنے کی تصدیق کرتے ہوئے مزید کارروائی کے لیے بنگلہ دیشی وزارت خارجہ کو روانہ کر دیا ہے۔

اگست 2024 میں ملک گیر عوامی احتجاج کے نتیجے میں اقتدار سے ہٹائے جانے کے بعد شیخ حسینہ ڈھاکہ سے فرار ہو کر دہلی پہنچی تھیں اور تب سے وہ وہیں مقیم ہیں۔ معزولی کے فوراً بعد بنگلہ دیش کی عبوری حکومت نے ان کے تمام سفری دستاویزات منسوخ کر دیے تھے۔ سال 2025 میں ڈھاکہ کی ایک عدالت نے طلبہ کے خلاف کریک ڈاؤن کے معاملے میں انھیں انسانیت کے خلاف جرائم کا مرتکب قرار دیتے ہوئے سزائے موت سنائی تھی، جسے شیخ حسینہ نے متعصبانہ اور سیاسی قرار دے کر مسترد کر دیا تھا۔

بنگلہ دیشی حکومت نے اس پاسپورٹ کی درخواست کو ایک محض سیاسی حربہ قرار دیا ہے۔ ڈھاکہ کے چیف پراسیکیوٹر محمد امین الاسلام کے مطابق سابق وزیر اعظم قانونی راستے سے واپسی کے لیے مطلوبہ اقدامات نہیں کر رہیں۔ ادھر خارجہ امور کے وزیر مملکت ہمایوں کبیر نے سخت ردعمل دیتے ہوئے شیخ حسینہ کو مفرور دہشت گرد اور ڈکٹیٹر قرار دیا اور کہا کہ ملک دہشت گردوں کو پاسپورٹ جاری نہیں کرتا۔ حکومت چاہتی ہے کہ وہ دونوں ممالک کے مابین مجرموں کی حوالگی کے معاہدے کے تحت واپس آکر عدالت میں پیش ہوں۔

دوسری جانب شیخ حسینہ کی جماعت عوامی لیگ نے الزام لگایا ہے کہ موجودہ حکومت ان سے خوفزدہ ہے اور اسی وجہ سے سفری دستاویزات فراہم کرنے سے گریز کر رہی ہے۔ مبصرین کا کہنا ہے کہ اس صورتحال نے نئی دہلی اور ڈھاکہ کے درمیان سفارتی تعلقات میں کشیدگی پیدا کر رکھی ہے کیونکہ بنگلہ دیشی حکومت چاہتی ہے کہ وہ ایک مجرم کی حیثیت سے قانون کا سامنا کریں جبکہ شیخ حسینہ کے اس اقدام سے ان کے حامیوں میں نئی توانائی پیدا کرنے کی کوشش سمجھی جا رہی ہے۔

stories.title: Oxford Museum Returns Ancestral Naga Remains to Community Delegates
stories.summary:
On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum at Oxford University formally returned the ancestral human remains of 39 individuals to representatives of the Naga community. Nearly 30 delegates originating from the mountainous northeastern Indian state of Nagaland, which shares a border with Myanmar, traveled to Britain to participate in the handover ceremony. Museum director Laura Van Broekhoven described the event as a historic milestone for all involved. This repatriation effort aligns with an ongoing international trend where Western ethnographic institutions reevaluate their artifact acquisition histories and return human remains to their Indigenous points of origin.

The Pitt Rivers Museum, established during the 19th century inside a Victorian Gothic building, houses the world's largest collection of Naga cultural objects, numbering over 6,000 items. The returned remains, primarily skulls accumulated between 1910 and 1940 predominantly through colonial administrators who also functioned as anthropologists, were officially signed over during a formal agreement. Museum documentation indicates that items and remains from this specific era were frequently seized during punitive military expeditions rather than acquired via voluntary gifts. Although the museum ceased displaying human remains back in 2020, approximately 2,700 additional remains still remain stored within its facilities due to past collection ethics that modern standards view as problematic.

Following the ceremony, the returned remains were immediately transported toward Heathrow Airport to begin their journey back to India. Tribal leaders, including 73-year-old Thejao Vihienuo who wore a traditional shawl, coordinated with the institution over a six-year period to finalize the delicate process. The delegation plans to inter the remains collectively beneath a joint memorial park in Nagaland so they can finally rest respectfully. Anthropologist Dolly Kikon noted that the collection includes the head of a traditional village chief, highlighting the complex historical context of the community's past traditions alongside the grief surrounding how the remains were originally removed.

stories.title: Trump Says FBI Is Investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Over China Ties
stories.summary:
United States President Donald Trump stated on Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang regarding an affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Trump mentioned he was amazed by the allegations involving Huang, whom he considers one of his closest Silicon Valley allies, adding that the CEO claimed he was unaware of the woman's espionage ties and that he believes Huang will be in good shape.

The announcement follows an internal investigation launched by Nvidia's board on Sunday to determine if the 63-year-old CEO was targeted by foreign intelligence efforts. Nvidia shares closed down more than 4% on Monday following the news. Huang reportedly informed employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife without providing details. Shareholders also filed a proposed class action lawsuit on Monday accusing Huang and the company of concealing his relationship with the suspected spy.

The New York Times previously reported that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who was investigated by US authorities and concluded to be a Chinese intelligence asset. The Chinese Foreign Ministry dismissed the narrative as a groundless accusation and smear. Meanwhile, US lawmakers and analysts noted that the development could prompt stricter congressional legislation regarding AI chip sales to China, though most analysts do not expect the longtime CEO to step down.

Huang maintains a 3.6% stake as Nvidia's fifth-largest shareholder. The investigation comes months after President Trump praised Huang and awarded him the National Medal of Science in October, on the same day Trump disclosed financial trades involving Nvidia stock.

stories.title: Nadira Magsi and Dania Patel Triumph at Thal Desert Jeep Rally
stories.summary:
The 11th edition of the Thal Desert Jeep Rally concluded on Sunday night, celebrating top racing talents during a vibrant closing ceremony held at the Yadgar Club in Muzaffargarh. Renowned racer Mir Nadir Magsi emerged victorious by capturing the first position in the men's Prepared Category. Meanwhile, Dania Patel delivered an impressive performance to claim the top spot in the women's Prepared Category. The concluding festivities drew a substantial gathering of race enthusiasts, distinguished dignitaries, and competing drivers.

Additional competitive results across the various race categories highlighted exceptional driving skills throughout the demanding desert tracks. In the remaining segments of the Prepared Category, Arbab Khan triumphed in Category B, Umar Iqbal Kanjo secured victory in Category C, and Zafar Baloch finished first in Category D. Furthermore, strong competitive displays were observed within the Stock Category, where Syed Asif Imam, Rab Nawaz Joiya, Hassan Jhandeer, Falak Sher Baloch, and female racer Ayla Malik all secured prominent placements through their notable racing proficiencies.

The event officially concluded with officials from the Tourism Development Corporation of Punjab (TDCP) distributing trophies and accolades among the successful drivers. To cap off the celebratory night, organizers arranged a spectacular fireworks display that illuminated the sky above Muzaffargarh, successfully wrapping up the multi-day desert motorsport competition.

stories.title: Pakistan LPG Marketers Association Postpones Strike After Official Talks
stories.summary:
The Pakistan LPG Marketers Association (PLPGMA) officially postponed its planned strike, which had been scheduled for November 16, following a productive negotiation meeting in Karachi on Monday. The impending strike was initially organized to protest a lack of stakeholder consultation regarding the government's newly announced liquefied petroleum gas policy. Sindh Governor Syed Nehal Hashmi hosted the delegation alongside Minister of State Kheal Das Kohistani and National Assembly Member Shahbaz Babar to address critical fuel supply dynamics amidst broader Middle East tensions and domestic energy challenges.

During the discussions, PLPGMA Senior Vice President Ali Haider emphasized that incorporating input from industry stakeholders is essential for formulating practical and effective energy policies. While Governor Hashmi assured the association that their grievances would be communicated directly to the relevant ministry, consumer financial pressures remain severe. Households, public transport operators using buses, minibuses, and rickshaws, as well as outdoor dining establishments have faced high consumer prices ranging from Rs500 to Rs550 per kilogram over recent months, alongside rising food and transport fares.

Official data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics indicates that national LPG import expenditures reached $285 million during the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, marking a 22 percent increase compared to $235 million during the same period last year. Mr. Haider pointed out that while the government introduced a policy intended to lower gas prices, market realities have kept costs elevated, urging the administration to reduce import duties and taxes to provide public relief. He added that international contract prices could potentially decrease in December if the ongoing conflict involving the United States and Iran subsides, though winter demand increases necessitate proactive government solutions to prevent a severe domestic fuel crisis.

stories.title: Foreign Investment in Pakistan Government Securities Surpasses $700 Million
stories.summary:
Foreign investment in Pakistan Investment Bonds surpassed $500 million during the first four months of the 2026-27 fiscal year, driven by high returns on domestic bonds. Treasury bills also recorded inflows totaling $238 million between July and October of FY27. This surge follows a 50 basis point increase in the policy rate to 12 percent by the State Bank of Pakistan on October 26, creating strong appeal for both foreign and domestic investors.

According to State Bank data, total investments in PIBs reached $509.2 million for the July-October period, with October alone accounting for approximately $251 million. The United Arab Emirates led these investments with $395.7 million, followed by Bahrain with $80 million in PIBs and $72 million in treasury bills. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom emerged as the largest investor in T-bills with $80 million, while equity market inflows remained low at $124.4 million over the four-month timeframe.

The high returns are bolstered by a stable exchange rate maintained for over a year, rendering the investments nearly risk-free. However, financial experts note that these high yields have crowded out the private sector, which struggles to compete for costly bank financing. Concurrently, the government continues efforts to encourage commercial lending toward small and medium enterprises and the housing sector.

Pakistan remains under an International Monetary Fund program, which has provided economic stability and reduced overall risks, a status acknowledged by both the IMF and the World Bank alongside ongoing concerns regarding severe poverty. The robust influx of foreign capital aids government objectives to secure additional dollar sources despite anticipated high remittances of $45 billion for the fiscal year.

stories.title: Used Car Imports Via Gift Scheme Continue Despite Strict Government Curbs
stories.summary:
Imports of used cars under the gift scheme persist, with more than 2,000 units entering Pakistan in October despite strict government restrictions. Auto vendors report that these vehicles are acquired through payments to Japanese auction houses via hawala channels and unregulated domestic cash sales. Former Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers chairman Aamir Allawala noted that monthly imports rose sharply from just seven units in May to 2,238 units in September, demonstrating that official curbs have failed to halt the exploitation of overseas Pakistani schemes.

Simultaneously, completely built-up unit vehicle imports rose by 40 percent to $126 million during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, up from $90 million in the same period of the previous fiscal year. Industry representatives argue that the newly announced auto policy favors imports over local manufacturing, threatening approximately 1,200 domestic component manufacturing enterprises, 300,000 direct workers, and 1.5 million indirect jobs. PAAPAM Chairman Abdul Rehman Aizaz stated that the policy deviates from prior consultations held with the Ministry of Industries until June 2026.

The component manufacturing sector further criticizes the National Tariff Policy, asserting that its proposed 15 percent tariff on completely built-up units is disproportionately low compared to regional competitors such as India, Thailand, and Indonesia, which levy tariffs between 52 and 120 percent. Industry leaders warn that the current trajectory will trigger significant dollar outflows, tax shortfalls for the Federal Board of Revenue, and a rollback of localization efforts as vehicle assemblers opt for imported parts.

stories.title: Pakistan Records Modest Export Growth and Sharp Import Surge With North America
stories.summary:
Pakistan's merchandise exports to North America grew modestly by 4.65 percent to reach $1.826 billion during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, compared to $1.745 billion a year earlier. Conversely, imports from the region experienced a substantial surge of 60.58 percent, rising to $841.31 million from $523.91 million over the same period. State Bank of Pakistan data indicates that this import growth aligns with Islamabad's efforts to balance bilateral trade deficits under a specific agreement with the United States.

The trade developments occur amidst policy shifts by US President Donald Trump, who implemented additional tariffs while granting limited relief to Pakistan through a reciprocal framework. The United States continues to dominate North American trade, accounting for nearly 94 percent of Pakistan's exports to the region. Specifically, exports to the US rose 4.44 percent to $1.716 billion in the July-September quarter of FY27, while imports from the US jumped 45.44 percent to $659.23 million.

In contrast, export performance in other parts of the region varied. Exports to Canada increased marginally by 7.53 percent to $109.72 million in the first quarter of FY27, following a 2.3 percent decline in the preceding fiscal year. Beyond North America, Pakistan's exports to Latin America sharply increased by 118.64 percent to $21.58 million, whereas exports to Central America remained nearly flat at $45.27 million, with Mexico serving as the primary destination.

stories.title: FPCCI Urges Industrial Tariff Rationalization to Prevent Demographic Disaster
stories.summary:
A leader of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry has called for a comprehensive rationalization of industrial energy tariffs to align with regional competitors and secure an affordable power supply. Adeel Siddiqui, a member of the FPCCI Executive Committee from Hyderabad, urged authorities to simplify the technology-driven tax regime, eliminate harassment for export-oriented sectors, and establish targeted, subsidised financing windows through the State Bank of Pakistan.

Siddiqui warned that the government is failing to capitalize on Pakistan's primary economic advantage—the cheapest labor in the region. He noted that Pakistan's labor costs are approximately 34 percent cheaper than India, 41 percent cheaper than Vietnam, and 62 percent cheaper than China. Without structural alignment, he cautioned, the country's demographic dividend risks turning into a demographic disaster akin to the missed opportunities of the past.

According to the FPCCI official, Pakistan's labor advantage is currently neutralized by what he termed the 'Big 3 trouble alignments': an energy pricing crisis, a complex taxation system, and high interest rates and operational costs. The appeal highlights the urgent need for structural reforms to foster manufacturing growth and bolster export competitiveness amidst ongoing industrial challenges.

stories.title: DawnMedia to Host Insurance Summit in Karachi Next Month
stories.summary:
DawnMedia has announced plans to host a major conference addressing the condition and upcoming direction of the nation's insurance sector. The event, designated as the Insurance Summit 2026, is scheduled to take place in Karachi on December 2. 

According to an official release, the upcoming gathering will convene industry experts, regulators, policymakers, insurance providers, and business leaders. Attendees will focus on discussing financial protection, risk coverage, and the overall future of the sector. A primary motivation for the event is that the nation's insurance penetration currently sits at under one percent of the gross domestic product, making the expansion of financial security a notable national hurdle. 

Organizers noted that the conference will tackle major obstacles restricting industry expansion, including public trust, accessibility, and limited awareness. Furthermore, discussions will examine ways to bolster coverage for households, individuals, and commercial enterprises. The scheduled agenda encompasses topics such as regulatory reforms, the local insurance landscape, risk management, reinsurance, policyholder protection, consumer trust, and claims, alongside digital innovation, microinsurance, and climate-risk coverage. 

Through cross-sector collaboration, dialogue, and the sharing of knowledge, the initiative strives to map out a course toward a resilient and accessible insurance framework within Pakistan. The Federal Insurance Ombudsman serves as the principal partner for this DawnMedia project. Additional backing comes from supporting partners TPL, Jubilee Life, Jubilee General, EFU Life, and IGI Life, as well as knowledge partners including the Securities & Exchange Commission of Pakistan and the Pakistan Business Council.

stories.title: Opposition Demands Talks and Access to Protesters in AJK
stories.summary:
The primary opposition alliance in Pakistan urged immediate dialogue with the Joint Awami Action Committee on Monday. The appeal followed an incident where a delegation from the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan was blocked at Kahuta while attempting to visit Azad Jammu and Kashmir to meet demonstrators, assess conditions, and express solidarity. According to TTAP spokesperson Hussein Ahmed Yousafzai, authorities provided no valid justification for preventing a peaceful political delegation from reaching the public.

The alliance demanded practical progress on public demands alongside an unbiased investigation into allegations regarding the unnecessary application of force. Additionally, officials called for injured individuals to receive top-tier medical care, proper legal access for arrested persons, and unrestricted entry into AJK for social and political figures. Organizers emphasized that the Kashmiri population does not stand alone in their struggles and vowed to champion their democratic and human rights across every legal and constitutional platform.

The situation highlights ongoing political tensions surrounding demonstrations in the region, which previously witnessed major shutterdown and wheeljam strikes on May 10, 2024. Opposition leaders stress that meaningful communication is essential to resolving the crisis peacefully. Government authorities have yet to respond publicly to the latest demands for unhindered access and formal discussions.

Providing a resolution to the unrest remains critical for regional stability and public safety. Observers note that addressing the core grievances of protesters through transparent channels will help prevent further escalations. The alliance maintains that safeguarding basic democratic liberties is a priority that requires immediate administrative attention.

stories.title: G7 Foreign Ministers Meet in Paris to Discuss Ukraine and Iran
stories.summary:
Top diplomats from the G7 industrialised nations gathered in Paris on Monday for a two-day meeting. European foreign ministers planned to urge US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to ensure that any forthcoming settlement to the conflict in Ukraine is fair to Kyiv and to prevent any escalation involving Iran. The discussions involve representatives from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the United States, offering a vital platform for European allies to voice strategic concerns.

The talks coincide with US-mediated negotiations scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the war in Russia and Ukraine. European leaders have expressed anxiety that Kyiv might be pushed into disadvantageous terms or that Washington could establish new security agreements with Moscow without European participation. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul stressed that Europe must retain a seat at the table and does not require a newly engineered security framework without input.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga is scheduled to join the Paris talks on Tuesday to address de-escalation, air defense protection, and Black Sea navigation. Meanwhile, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot noted that European representatives would also take part in the Abu Dhabi discussions. President Volodymyr Zelensky coordinated positions with European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen ahead of the diplomatic engagements.

The outcome of these high-level meetings could significantly shape post-war European security architecture and transatlantic relations. Secretary Rubio noted prior to his departure that European security infrastructure has consistently remained a primary topic in ongoing negotiation discussions. Allies continue to emphasize unity and collective engagement to address these pressing geopolitical challenges.

stories.title: Saud Shakeel and Debutant Saqib Put Pakistan Ahead in First Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan closed the second day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in a strong position at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, reducing the visitors to 114-3 after declaring their first innings at 434-9. Sri Lanka ended the day trailing by 320 runs with seven wickets remaining in hand.

Sri Lanka suffered a troubled start when seasoned pacer Mohammad Abbas removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck in the third over, followed by 31-year-old debutant Saqib Khan dismissing Dinesh Chandimal in the fourth over to leave the visitors at 12-2. Lahiru Udara and skipper Kamindu Mendis then stabilized the innings with a 53-run partnership before Saqib dismissed Lahiru for 42. At stumps, Mendis was batting on 40 alongside Dhananjaya de Silva on 22, with their unbroken partnership standing at 49 runs.

Earlier in the day, Pakistan resumed their innings from 281-5 and added 153 runs before declaring after 106.3 overs. Saud Shakeel missed his fifth Test century by just seven runs, getting caught behind off Asitha Fernando for 93 runs from 199 deliveries. Wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori contributed 48 runs, forming a vital 96-run sixth-wicket partnership with Saud. Debutant Arafat Minhas also performed strongly, scoring an attacking 52 from 72 balls before the declaration.

Saqib Khan finished a successful debut day with bowling figures of 2-54 in 10.1 overs for Pakistan. For Sri Lanka, Asitha Fernando and Dilshan Madushanka claimed three wickets each, while Lahiru Kumara and Milan Rathnayaka secured one wicket apiece.

stories.title: امریکی صدر ٹرمپ کا قطر کے وزیراعظم سے ملاقات کے بعد ایران پر مزید حملے روکنے کا اعلان
stories.summary:
امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے قطر کے وزیرِ اعظم شیخ محمد بن عبدالرحمن آل ثانی سے وائٹ ہاؤس میں ملاقات کے بعد ایران کے خلاف مزید فوجی حملے فی الحال روکنے کا اعلان کیا ہے۔ صدر ٹرمپ کے مطابق، یہ فیصلہ قطر، سعودی عرب، متحدہ عرب امارات، بحرین اور کویت سمیت خطے کے دیگر ممالک کے رہنماؤں کی درخواست پر کیا گیا ہے جو خطے میں امن چاہتے ہیں اور نئے حملوں کے مخالف ہیں۔
